approachQuestion.prompt:
Repeated signal multiplier

Return a^e modulo m in [0,m-1]. Define a^0=1, including a=0.

Example 1: a=7,e=13,m=100 -> 7.
Example 2: a=0,e=0,m=9 -> 1.
Example 3: a=8,e=0,m=1 -> 0.

Constraints and assumptions: 0 <= a <= 10^9; 0 <= e <= 10^18; 1 <= m <= 10^9. Do not construct the full power. Products of two residues fit signed 64-bit integers. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Use a modular accumulator initialized to 1 mod m and base=a mod m. At each step multiply the accumulator by base if the exponent is odd, square base, and halve the exponent. Reduce each product modulo m.
options.feedback: Removing an odd factor and squaring for the remaining half preserves the power, including zero exponent and modulus one.

options.text: Start at 1 mod m and multiply by a modulo m exactly e times.
options.feedback: The result is correct and bounded, but the method does not reuse squared powers.

options.text: Replace e with e mod m before computing the power modulo m.
options.feedback: For a=2,e=3,m=3 this gives 1 rather than 2. This exponent reduction has no general justification.

options.text: Return (a*e) mod m, using safe wider arithmetic if needed.
options.feedback: Even with exact arithmetic, a=3,e=2,m=10 yields 6 rather than 9.

feedback.reason: Halve an exponent while preserving a modular-power invariant.
details: Set result=1 mod m, base=a mod m, remaining=e. While remaining>0, multiply result by base modulo m if remaining is odd, square base modulo m, and halve remaining with floor division.
Odd exponent bits contribute the current base, then squaring and halving preserve the remaining power. Reduce residues after multiplication as specified. Exponent zero returns 1 mod m, including m=1.

“Use a modular accumulator initialized to 1 mod m and base=a mod m. At each step multiply the accumulator by base if the exponent is odd, square base, and halve the exponent. Reduce each product modulo m.”: Removing an odd factor and squaring for the remaining half preserves the power, including zero exponent and modulus one.
“Start at 1 mod m and multiply by a modulo m exactly e times.”: The result is correct and bounded, but the method does not reuse squared powers.
“Replace e with e mod m before computing the power modulo m.”: For a=2,e=3,m=3 this gives 1 rather than 2. This exponent reduction has no general justification.
“Return (a*e) mod m, using safe wider arithmetic if needed.”: Even with exact arithmetic, a=3,e=2,m=10 yields 6 rather than 9.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (iterative-squaring). Let e be the original exponent. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

options.text: O(1 + log(e + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(1 + log(e + 1)) time, O(1 + log(e + 1)) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One modular update round per exponent bit uses constant word state.
details: Each iteration halves the remaining exponent, so there is one iteration per binary digit when e>0. Constant many words are kept, with no recursion. The zero-exponent case takes constant work.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(1 + log(e + 1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct, including e=0.
“O(e + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes one multiplication per factor, not halving.
“O(1 + log(e + 1)) time, O(1 + log(e + 1)) auxiliary space”: The iterative method saves no power history.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The halving loop grows with the exponent bit length.

methodReveal.title: Square and halve
methodReveal.description: Set result=1 mod m, base=a mod m, remaining=e. While remaining>0, multiply result by base modulo m if remaining is odd, square base modulo m, and halve remaining with floor division.
